chapter: Streetcar, Cab revival shows and trips abroad
title: The bootleg Fletcher Henderson in the 1950s album
summary: An unauthorised album from the Cafe Society engagement features him and Dick Vance, with most tunes and arrangements his; he cannot trace the label.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: So anyway, after Fletcher got sick, then I took the band over for the rest of the engagement. In fact, there's an album out now -- Fletcher Henderson in the '50s, and, of course, nobody knows who put it out, and I've taken it to the union --
: What label is it on, one of these bootleg labels?
I haven't seen it. But you're on it?
And it's got -- I'm on it, me and Dick Vance and the same group I just named is on it, and most of the tunes are my compositions. And --
: You can't trace it down, huh?
And most all the arrangements are mine.
: What's the name of the label? Do you know?
It's on a big, yellow thing. I have it at home happen to know, because I tell you, Jeff got it, pulled it out one day when I was over to Goodies. You know Goodies?
And then -- something else you wanted to say?
No, I was just going to say that the, you know, I guess Dick Vance had been with Fletcher from way, way back.
